method: Started from the market-wide screen of XBRL pay-versus-performance tables (companies whose own tables show both a CEO change and a large loss on $100 invested). For the departed CEOs at the well-known names on that list (PayPal, Illumina, DocuSign, Twilio, Match, Pinterest, Teladoc, Chegg, Novavax, Dentsply Sirona, Five9, Boston Beer, Bausch Health, Opendoor, QuantumScape, SolarEdge, Fate, FIS, MarketAxess, STAAR, Harley-Davidson, Zillow, UiPath, GitLab, Kohl's, Lucid), read the departure 8-K (item 5.02) and its exhibits, then the first proxy after the exit for actual separation amounts (Summary Compensation Table footnotes, separation/transition/retirement sections, actual-termination tables), falling back to the potential-payments table only where nothing actual exists (basis estimated). Where a company had more than one CEO depart (Dentsply Sirona, Opendoor, STAAR, Chegg), each departure with disclosed terms is its own case. Zero-pay outcomes are recorded only where a filing says so. Stock: the company's own value of $100 from its 10-K performance-graph table where the 10-K prints values, otherwise its proxy pay-versus-performance table; the window starts and ends inside the CEO tenure, longest available, ties broken by the later end date; null when every table starts before the CEO took over. Pay fields hold single filed figures; when a filing prints no total, total is the sum of the disclosed items described in notes. Lyft and Kohl's Gass/Buchanan are covered by other slices; the screen's smaller or secondary names (e.g. BRC Group, American Bitcoin, Gogo, Cambium, Republic Airways, Amylyx, BioMarin, GameStop, Flagstar, Americold, LyondellBasell, lululemon, NovoCure, EPAM) were not researched here.
